catalog_quote: [p.87] Previous sections have analyzed the consonant and vocalic systems of Western Sisaala's segmental phonology. This section describes the suprasegmental features utilized in the language. This will include tone and intonation. ... [p.89] As we will see, much of the tonal system of Western Sisaala can be marked as no tone, contrasting with high tone. There is no midlevel tone in Western Sisaala, therefore leaving a binary distinction between high and low. In Western Sisaala's register tone system, high and low tones appear on the syllable. Tone appears when lexical or grammatical distinctions are necessary between lexical items or grammatical functions or when the tone was perceptually clear to the researcher. When no tone is given, the syllable is considered toneless, or low. ... [p.91] In Western Sisaala a multisyllabic morpheme may contain a high or low tone on each syllable. The …

audit.reasoning: The deciding quotation is verbatim in the held Moran 2006 thesis at pp.87, 89, 91 (checked on page scan; text is garbled). Moran 2006 (and its 2008 VDM reprint) is the only linguistic description of Western Sisaala: Moran himself reports no prior materials (p.23), Glottolog lists nothing else for west2465, and the Rowland & Rowland 1965 phonology in our ref list is Glottolog-curated as Sisaala-Tumulung [sil], i.e. a different languoid (auto-assigned to ssl only by the langsci importer). The author's own later 117-pp. draft grammar (2009, downloaded now from his GitHub and repeats the two-tone H vs unmarked-L analysis with lexical and grammatical tone and again says nothing about word stress, so 'tonal, stress/domain not stated by the source' (tonal-OR-pitch accent rather than no word stress) remains exactly what the sources support. sources.quote: p.13: 'Isaalo is a tone language that uses differences in relative frequency to convey lexical and grammatical distinctions. Tones may be high or low ... In Isaalo, high tone is contrastive and is therefore marked on lexical items with an acute accent'. p.24: 'Isaalo has a two tone system, high and low. The low tone is the unmarked case ... High tone on forms is both lexically and grammatically contrastive' (basa 'mat' vs basá 'chair'; e 2S vs é 2PL; natawa/natawá sg/pl; m bo / m bó PRES/PST). sources.note: Citing works (Mustapha 2018: 4-5, drawing on Luri 2009, Toupin 1995 and Moran 2006) report that Sɩsaalɩ is a tone language with lexical and grammatical tone (two tones, H vs L; verbs L in the present vs H on the final syllable in the past; tone distinguishes pronouns and imperatives), nine phonemic vowels with ATR harmony; as the only dedicated phonology thesis on the Sisaala cluster after Rowland & Rowland 1965 it very likely contains a tone chapter (inventory, tonal processes, grammatical tone).
